senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; גדד, cmp. גזר)decree, fate, esp. Gad (Fortune), a god worshipped by the Babylonians and the Jewish exiles.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 63b:10">Snh. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳ נמי מיכתב כתיב</he> Gad is also one of the names of idols mentioned in the Bible.
<cite ref="Shabbat 67b:1">Sabb. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳ אינו אלא לשון ע״א</he> Gad is nothing else than a designation of an idol, v. <cite ref="C00156">next w.</cite>

senses.gloss: גַּד יָוָן pr. n. Gad Yavan (Greek Fortune) near Jerusalem.
units: Zab. I, 5 כְּמִן ג׳ י׳ לשילוה as long as it takes from G. Y. to Siloah; Tosef. ib. I, 10 כְּמִגַּדְיָוָן לשילה; Snh. 63ᵇ כְּמִיגַּדְיָוָן לשילה (corr. acc.)—[Gad Yavan is prob. the name of a pool connected with the Siloah, perh. Fount of the Virgin, v. Sm. Bible Dict. s. v. Siloam.] [Toh. VI, 6; Erub. 22ᵇ בית גד גד, v. גִּלְגּוּל.]
